pr_title: *: support the variable of `default_collation_for_utf8mb4` and corresponding behaviors
pr_body:
<!--

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/46384

Problem Summary:
https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_default_collation_for_utf8mb4

> The default utf8mb4 collation is used in the following statements:
> 
> 1. [SHOW COLLATION](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/show-collation.html) and [SHOW CHARACTER SET](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/show-character-set.html).
> 
> 2. [CREATE TABLE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-table.html) and [ALTER TABLE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/alter-table.html) having a CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 clause without a COLLATION clause, either for the table character set or for a column character set.
> 
> 3. [CREATE DATABASE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/create-database.html) and [ALTER DATABASE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/alter-database.html) having a CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 clause without a COLLATION clause.
> 
> 4. Any statement containing a string literal of the form _utf8mb4'some text' without a COLLATE clause.


### What is changed and how it works?
* Support the variable of `default_collation_for_utf8mb4 `
* Support show collation and show character set
* Support `create/alter table` behaviors
* Support `create/alter database` behaviors
* This PR doesn't support item 4.

issue_context.body:
* Support the variable of `default_collation_for_utf8mb4 `
* Support show collation and show character set
* Support `create/alter table` behaviors
* Support `create/alter database` behaviors

review_comments:
IMHO it's weird to allow a `cs` parameter for `getDefaultCollationForUTF8MB4` and it returns nothing when `cs != 'utf8mb4'`.

For example, the [code above](https://github.com/zimulala/tidb/blob/2de36755d11812c0a99ce893871370895c92e5e8/ddl/ddl_api.go#L150-L151) confused me at the first glance:

```
	if !explicitCollation && explicitCharset {
		coll, err := getDefaultCollationForUTF8MB4(ctx.GetSessionVars(), charsetOpt.Chs)
```

Could you consider removing this new function and just merge the logic to `charset.GetDefaultCollation`?
`charset. GetDefaultCollation` places many, this function(`getDefaultCollationForUTF8MB4`) is used and the function affects only DDL operations. So we can't put this function in

Why is this function in `ddl` package, but not in `charset` package?

I suggest to modify the current `charset.GetDefaultCollation`, add an argument `sessVars`. We have only 10+ reference to the `charset.GetDefaultCollation`, and most of them have `sctx` in the environment, so I think it won't be a big change to do this refractor. But I'm not sure whether it's the expected behavior... I see this PR doesn't touch the `expression` package, but `(*convertFunctionClass).getFunction` will also call `GetDefaultCollation`. Is it expected?

Besides the `GetDefaultCollation`, I also found `GetDefaultCollationLegacy` used in parser. I'm not sure whether it should also be modified :thinking: .
I put it here because it is currently only used for DDL operations, and the PR description explains the scope of this variable's influence, that is, it should not affect the expression.

> it should not affect the expression

Well this actually affects the expression, we should expect the following result:

```
tidb> set @@default_collation_for_utf8mb4='utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci';
Query OK, 0 rows affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

tidb> select _utf8mb4'a' = _utf8mb4'A', _utf8mb4'a' = _utf8mb4'a  ';
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
| _utf8mb4'a' = _utf8mb4'A' | _utf8mb4'a' = _utf8mb4'a  ' |
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
|                         1 |                           0 |
+---------------------------+-----------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

As mentioned in the PR desc:

> Any statement containing a string literal of the form _utf8mb4'some text' without a COLLATE clause.

So I think @YangKeao 's comment is reasonable.
Yes, as I said above, currently only DDL is affected, and PR also describes that "This PR doesn't support item 4."
